questions.q: What makes Kinesis Data Analytics different from Athena or Redshift?
options: It processes data directly from a stream while it's still in motion, rather than querying data already at rest
It can only query data that has already been loaded into Redshift
It replaces the need for Kinesis Data Streams entirely
It only supports batch jobs run once per day
questions.explain: Kinesis Data Analytics reads directly from a Kinesis stream (or Firehose) and runs continuous processing on arriving records, before anything is written to storage.

questions.q: What are the two ways to write processing logic in Kinesis Data Analytics?
options: A SQL application model, and Apache Flink (Java/Python/Scala)
Only Python scripts uploaded through the console
Only drag-and-drop visual pipelines
Excel formulas imported via S3
questions.explain: You can write continuous SQL queries, or use the Apache Flink runtime for a full programming model — AWS now brands the Flink runtime as Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink.

questions.q: What is a 'windowed aggregation' in stream processing?
options: A metric computed over a rolling slice of stream time, emitting fresh results as each window closes
A one-time SQL query run against a finished, static dataset
A method for compressing records before storage
A way to permanently stop a stream from receiving new records
questions.explain: Windowed aggregations — tumbling or sliding — compute continuously over a moving time slice, which is what makes real-time metrics like 'orders per minute' possible.

questions.q: What has AWS renamed its Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics runtime to?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
AWS Stream Processor Pro
Amazon Flink Data Warehouse
AWS EventBridge Analytics
questions.explain: AWS rebranded the Flink runtime as Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, shifting its primary emphasis there while the original SQL application model remains available.

questions.q: Where can Kinesis Data Analytics send its processed output?
options: Back to another stream, to a Firehose delivery stream, or to a Lambda function
Only directly to a printer
Nowhere — it can only display results in the AWS console
Only to an on-premises database over a VPN
questions.explain: Processed results are typically written back out to a Kinesis stream, a Firehose delivery stream, or invoked via Lambda for further handling.
